title: Protocol and Signal
premise: Navigator Emrys Almeida discovers his own name on the cargo manifest of the Halcyon Reach, a colony ship officially listed as never launched—yet he has fragmented memories of its voyage and the massacre of its 4,000 sleepers. The shipping conglomerate Veyra Combine erased the ship to bury a failed terraforming gamble, and the 'backups' in his hold are actually survivors' minds the Combine wants destroyed before a corporate audit. Hunted by Combine enforcers and betrayed by the mentor who sold his memories to him in the first place, Emrys must broadcast the ship's sealed flight recorder from inside contested space. He succeeds at devastating cost—his closest ally dies holding the relay—and the truth detonates across the colonies, toppling the Combine and forcing Emrys to decide whether the sleeping backups, including a copy of the sister he lost, deserve to be woken into a world that finally remembers them.
about_author: Marguerite Yarrow is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to ships that never answered. She writes science fiction about the people history files under 'lost with all hands.'

chapters.title: The Manifest That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Emrys Almeida's POV. Running routine cargo through contested orbits, Emrys audits a client's manifest and finds his own name listed on the Halcyon Reach, a colony ship the registry insists never flew. He tells himself it's a clerical ghost, but his hands shake. The beat is quiet dread: the past knocking on a door he sealed.

chapters.title: Backups in the Hold
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. He inspects the cryo-crates his employer ordered him never to open and finds they carry neural backups—thousands of them—tagged with Halcyon Reach passenger IDs. His fragmented dreams of a burning corridor suddenly feel like evidence. The beat is the first crack in his carefully maintained invisibility.

chapters.title: Five Years of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Emrys POV, with flashback. A slow transit gives him room to remember how he bought his way off-grid after the war: a memory broker, a mentor named Ilsa Voss, a past he chose to forget. He realizes the gaps in his memory align with the Halcyon's flight dates. The beat is reluctant self-confrontation.

chapters.title: The Auditor
chapters.summary: Introduce Sef Okonkwo, a Combine compliance auditor POV. Okonkwo is sent to quietly retrieve the mislabeled crates before the sector audit, and flags Emrys as a loose end. We see the Combine's machinery from inside: efficient, courteous, murderous. The beat is menace wearing a lanyard.

chapters.title: Docking Bay Interrogation
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Combine enforcers board his ship for a 'routine inspection.' Emrys survives by playing dumb and hiding one crate's access chip in his prosthetic eye socket, but they take his nav logs. The beat is terror managed through competence—he realizes he's already a suspect.

chapters.title: Ilsa Voss Knows
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Emrys confronts Ilsa, his old broker and mentor, who admits the Halcyon Reach existed and that she sold him his own amnesia as a favor. She begs him to let it stay buried, revealing the massacre killed 4,000 sleepers and the Combine's terraforming colony died with them. The beat is betrayal by the person who saved him.

chapters.title: What the Recorder Remembers
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Using the access chip, he partially decrypts the ship's black box: crew logs showing the Combine deliberately vented the sleeper decks to hide a colony failure, then erased the launch. He now holds the only proof. The beat is the burden of knowing—truth as a weight, not a weapon.

chapters.title: The Man Who Never Flew
chapters.summary: Okonkwo POV. Okonkwo discovers Emrys's name was on the original crew roster—Emrys was the Halcyon's junior navigator who escaped in a lifepod. He reports that the witness is the ghost himself. The beat is the hunter realizing the prey is also the crime's last survivor.

chapters.title: Allies in Contested Space
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. He reaches the free-station port of Ceres Verge and recruits allies: Dara, a pirate-archivist who owes him, and Toma, his engineer and only friend, who insists on coming despite the risk. They plan to broadcast the recorder through the sector relay. The beat is chosen family forming under threat.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The Combine offers Emrys full amnesty, a new identity, and restoration of his erased memories—if he surrenders the recorder. Tempted by the promise of wholeness, he nearly accepts, then realizes they'll kill him once he's irrelevant. The beat is temptation resisted at the edge of despair.

chapters.title: Dara's Archive
chapters.summary: Dara POV. Dara verifies the black box data against salvaged debris fields and finds physical corroboration: the Halcyon's hull, scuttled in a debris belt, with vent-burn patterns on the sleeper decks. The massacre becomes fact, not claim. The beat is grim vindication—and the knowledge that proof this good makes them all targets.

chapters.title: Audit Day
chapters.summary: Okonkwo POV. The sector audit begins; Okonkwo's superiors order him to falsify the crate inventory, and he hesitates for the first time. His quiet integrity starts to turn. The beat is a functionary's conscience flickering awake inside the machine.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Belt
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Enforcers ambush their ship in the debris belt while Dara's team recovers hull evidence. Toma is gravely wounded holding the airlock; they escape but lose the evidence cache. The beat is the cost of the mission becoming real and personal.

chapters.title: Toma's Vigil
chapters.summary: Emrys POV, hospital bay on Ceres Verge. Toma drifts in and out, and between lucid moments urges Emrys to broadcast even if it kills them both. Emrys confesses his guilt: he was on the Halcyon's crew and ran while the decks vented. The beat is guilt spoken aloud at last, and forgiveness he can't yet accept.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Offer
chapters.summary: Okonkwo POV. Unable to falsify the audit cleanly, Okonkwo secretly copies the falsification orders and contacts Emrys, offering the Combine's internal chain of command in exchange for protection. The hunter defects. The beat is loyalty inverted—an insider choosing truth over the institution that owns him.

chapters.title: Assembly of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys unlocks the hold's backups and discovers they aren't just passengers: they're testimony, each sleeper's final recorded hours preserved in their neural snapshots. Waking one—the ship's captain—gives a living witness. The beat is the dead given voices, and the horror of what they say.

chapters.title: The Relay Run
chapters.summary: Emrys POV, climax begins. The plan: thread contested space to the sector relay during the Combine's audit broadcast window. Ilsa, seeking redemption, provides the Combine's patrol schedule—but it's a trap she was forced to give up. The beat is hope laced with the certainty of betrayal.

chapters.title: Trap at Threshold Station
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The ambush springs; Ilsa is captured, Dara's ship is crippled, and Okonkwo's evidence is seized. Emrys escapes with the black box alone, hunted through the station's guts. The beat is everything collapsing—the plan's cost exceeding anyone's willingness to pay.

chapters.title: Toma's Stand
chapters.summary: Emrys POV, climax. Toma, dying, takes the crippled ship on a suicide run to jam the relay's defenses while Emrys broadcasts the recorder, the hull evidence, and the sleepers' testimony live across the sector. Toma's last transmission is a joke. The beat is sacrifice—loyalty fulfilled in the act of dying for truth.

chapters.title: Signal Received
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The broadcast lands: colonies riot, the audit collapses, Combine executives are arrested, and Okonkwo's copied orders become the prosecution's centerpiece. Ilsa testifies from custody. The beat is the world tilting—truth arriving too late for the dead, but not too late for the record.

chapters.title: The Question of the Sleepers
chapters.summary: Emrys POV, falling action. With the Combine fallen, Emrys faces the backups: 4,000 minds, including a snapshot of his sister, who died believing he abandoned them. Waking them means responsibility; keeping them asleep means another erasure. The beat is inheritance accepted—he is what remains of the Halcyon, and so is he.

chapters.title: Protocol and Signal
chapters.summary: Emrys POV, resolution. Months later, the first backups wake to a world that remembers them; Emrys, navigator again, pilots the refitted Halcyon Reach on its real maiden voyage, Toma's name on the hull and Ilsa's testimony in the archives. He finally reads his own full memory file and weeps, then sets course. The beat is earned peace: the signal carried, the protocol kept.
